title: Trauma-Informed Care
tagline: Safety first, always, for the wounded young.
welcome: Trauma changes the question from 'what is wrong with you?' to 'what happened to you?' This course rebuilds your entire practice around that question.
vignette: A twelve-year-old flinches when a teacher raises a book to shelve it. No one else notices. The trauma-informed counselor notices, and understands that the body keeps a calendar of its own. Care begins with safety the child can feel.
vignette_attr: A classroom trigger moment, drawn from practice
description: A comprehensive course in trauma-informed care with children and adolescents: trauma types and their developmental impact, neurobiology of trauma, the principles of safety and trust, trauma-informed relationships and environments, stabilization skills, and knowing when to refer for trauma-focused treatment.
questions: What has this child survived, and how does it show today?
How do I build safety a nervous system can believe?
When is stabilization enough, and when is specialized treatment needed?
importance: Trauma is common and largely unseen in young people
Trauma-informed care prevents re-traumatization by systems
Safety and relationship are the foundation of all trauma recovery
misconceptions: that trauma-informed care is a therapy, when it is a stance and system that precedes therapy
that children must narrate trauma to heal, when stabilization and safety come first
figures: whose work mapped how trauma lives in the body
whose neurosequential model guides regulation-first care
whose stages of recovery organize the field
outcomes: You will see trauma in behavior, body, and learning.
You will explain stress response and regulation to caregivers.
You will create environments a nervous system can trust.
You will regulate, relate, then reason, in that order.
You will train grounding and regulation with young people.
You will know the boundary of your role and the pathway beyond.
modules: Trauma Defined and Its Developmental Impact
Naming the wound is the first act of care.
Regulation and the window of tolerance
The brain story turns blame into understanding.
The principles audit every system the child touches.
Stabilization is the gift you can give immediately.
Referral and the Continuum of Trauma Treatment
Good referral is a trauma-informed skill.
practicum: Case formulation with a trauma lens
tips: Audit your own setting for hidden triggers
integration: Trauma-informed care reframes assessment, crisis, behavior, and family work across the programme.
faith: We bind up the wounded as an act of sacred hospitality, gentle and unhurried.
closing: May every wounded child find in you a place their nervous system can finally rest.
